alt: Timeline of the first phase of the armed struggle: bans and detentions in 1964, the Battle of Chinhoyi on 28 April 1966, the Wankie and Sipolilo campaigns of 1967-68 and ZANLA's reorganisation in 1970-72.
caption: Figure: timeline of the first phase, 1964-1972

alt: Timeline of the origins of the Cold War: Yalta in February 1945, Potsdam, Churchill's Iron Curtain speech in March 1946, the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan of 1947, the Berlin Blockade from June 1948 and NATO in April 1949.
caption: Figure: timeline of the origins of the Cold War, 1945-1949

alt: Timeline of Company rule: occupation in 1890, the 1898 Order in Council, settlers' elected majority in 1903, the 1918 land ruling, the referendum of 27 October 1922 and responsible government on 1 October 1923.
caption: Figure: timeline of Company rule in Southern Rhodesia

alt: Timeline of the French Revolution from the opening of the Estates-General on 5 May 1789 and the Bastille, through the republic of September 1792 and the king's execution on 21 January 1793, to Robespierre's fall in July 1794 and the coup of 18 Brumaire on 9 November 1799.
caption: Figure: key events of the French Revolution, 1789-1799

alt: Timeline of German unification: Bismarck becomes Minister-President in 1862, Prussia wins at Königgrätz on 3 July 1866, the Ems Telegram of 13 July 1870 leads to war and Sedan, and the Empire is proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871.
caption: Figure: timeline of German unification, 1861-1871

alt: Timeline of the July Crisis of 1914 from the Sarajevo assassination on 28 June, the German blank cheque and the Austrian ultimatum to Austria's declaration of war on 28 July, Russian mobilisation, and German and British declarations of war in early August.
caption: Figure: the July Crisis, 28 June-6 August 1914

alt: Timeline from the internal settlement of March 1978 and the Lusaka Commonwealth meeting of August 1979 to the opening of Lancaster House on 10 September, the agreement of 21 December 1979, the February 1980 election and independence on 18 April 1980.
caption: Figure: timeline of Lancaster House and independence

alt: Timeline of Mao's China from the 1950 Agrarian Reform Law and the First Five-Year Plan to the Great Leap Forward of 1958-62, the famine of 1959-61, the Cultural Revolution from 1966, Mao's death in September 1976 and the arrest of the Gang of Four.
caption: Figure: timeline of Mao's China, 1950-1976

alt: Schematic map of the consequences of the Mfecane: Mzilikazi's Ndebele to Zimbabwe, Zwangendaba across the Zambezi in 1835 to found Ngoni states, Nxaba north of the Zambezi, Soshangane's Gaza state in southern Mozambique, Sobhuza's Swazi, Sebetwane's Kololo in Barotseland and Moshoeshoe's Basotho in the Drakensberg.
caption: Figure: where the main groups went after the Zulu rise (schematic, not to scale)

alt: Timeline of the Mutapa state: Mutota's move north in about 1430-1450, Portuguese at Sofala in 1505, the treaty of 1607, Mavura's vassal status in 1629 and the Rozvi expulsion of the Portuguese in the late 1600s.
caption: Figure: timeline of the Mutapa state and the Portuguese

alt: Timeline of Nazi foreign policy: leaving the League in October 1933, conscription in 1935, the Rhineland in 1936, the Anschluss and Munich in 1938, the Nazi-Soviet Pact and the invasion of Poland in 1939 and Barbarossa on 22 June 1941.

alt: Timeline of the Ndebele state from Mzilikazi's break with Shaka in the 1820s and the crossing of the Limpopo in 1837-1839 to Lobengula's accession in 1870, the Rudd Concession of 1888 and the war of 1893-94.
caption: Figure: timeline of the Ndebele state

alt: Five groups of causes of the 1896-97 risings: long-term grievances (loss of land, cattle and independence; forced labour, taxes and the Native Police), the 1895-96 disasters, the opportunity of the Jameson Raid and religious leadership, all leading to the risings.
caption: Figure: grievances (grey), disasters (amber), opportunity (green) and leadership (blue) behind the 1896-97 risings

alt: Timeline of Russia from 1914 to 1917 with Western dates and old-style Russian dates: the March 1917 strikes and abdication, Lenin's return in April, the July Days, the Kornilov affair and the Bolshevik seizure of power on 7-8 November 1917.
caption: Figure: timeline of the Russian revolutions, 1914-1917

alt: Chart of SADC institutions: the Summit of Heads of State or Government above the Council of Ministers, the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security, the Secretariat in Gaborone and the SADC Tribunal, with National Committees and the Parliamentary Forum linking member states.
caption: Figure: institutions of SADC

alt: Timeline from the Rhodesian Front's election win in December 1962 and UDI on 11 November 1965 through sanctions, the 1969 constitution and the 1970 republic to the internal settlement of March 1978 and Muzorewa's premiership in June 1979.

alt: Chart of the six main organs of the United Nations: the General Assembly, the Security Council with its five permanent veto-holding members, the International Court of Justice, the Economic and Social Council, the Secretariat and the Trusteeship Council.
caption: Figure: the main organs of the United Nations

alt: Five long-term causes of the First World War: the alliance system of 1879 to 1907, militarism and the naval race, imperial and economic rivalry, the Balkans and war plans with nationalism, all leading to war in 1914.
caption: Figure: the long-term causes of the First World War

alt: Causes of the Second World War: Versailles grievances, the Depression, fascist and militarist expansion with League failures, and appeasement (long-term, grey), then the Anschluss, Munich, Prague and the Nazi-Soviet Pact (short-term, amber), leading to the invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939.
caption: Figure: long-term (grey) and short-term (amber) causes of the Second World War
